title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

title: Save Our Libraries
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Indivisible McHenry County is hosting a protest rally to show our opposition to the Trump administration's proposed elimination of the IMLS (Institute of Museum and Library Services), which will affect us on a local level. The rally will take place on Friday, June 20th, in front of the McHenry Public Library, 809 Front St (Rte 31), McHenry, from 3 p.m. until 5 p.m.

On June 6th, a Federal judge gave the Trump administration permission to proceed with dismantling the IMLS even though there is another lawsuit underway that is trying to save the agency through a different Federal court.

The IMLS was created and funded by Congress in 1996 for the purpose of providing support to libraries and museums in every state in the U.S. The agency has had bipartisan support throughout its history, with reauthorization occurring under the Clinton, George W. Bush, Obama, and Trump administrations. The IMLS is required by law to conduct activities that support libraries and to provide reports to Congress on important issues. The devastating cuts to the IMLS’s grants and services will make it impossible for the agency to operate as required by Congress. 

Although libraries in McHenry County do not rely on the IMLS for most of their funding, the elimination of the IMLS could still result in cuts to library services that are enjoyed by our residents and tens of thousands of other people in Illinois. The IMLS provides millions of dollars in funding to the Illinois State Library that is used to fund RAILS (Reaching Across Illinois Libraries System), the government agency that assists more than 4000 library facilities in Illinois, including all of the libraries in McHenry County.

RAILS provides the interlibrary delivery service which allows library patrons to check out books and other items from any library within the Illinois system. RAILS also provides: a shared electronic catalog and cataloging support • group purchases and member discounts that helps libraries to save money • continuing education and consulting resources to library employees and trustees • content services for online publishing • grant opportunities for local libraries • and many other valuable services. If the IMLS is eliminated it is unlikely that RAILS will be able to survive, and all of the valuable services that it provides to our residents will also be eliminated. Let your voice be heard. Please join us on June 20th.

description:
Ann Burroughs, International Human Rights Leader and President/CEO, Japanese American National Museum in Los Angeles

🗓️ Wednesday, July 2nd

📍 St. Andrew’s Episcopal Church – 4400 Barranca Pkwy, Irvine

🍕 Pizza Social @ 6:30 PM

🗣️ Meeting Begins @ 7:00 PM

💻 Hybrid Format: In-Person + Zoom

Join Democrats of Greater Irvine (DGI) for our July 2nd meeting as we welcome Ann Burroughs, president and CEO of the Japanese American National Museum (JANM) located in Los Angeles.

An internationally recognized human rights leader, Ann is also Chair of Amnesty International's Global Council, its highest decision-making body that brings together human rights leaders from over 70 countries.

Ann's life-long commitment to racial and social justice was shaped by her experience as a young anti-apartheid activist in her native South Africa where she was jailed as a political prisoner.

JANM has been in the forefront of speaking out when diversity, individual dignity and social justice are undermined by sharing lessons from the wrongful internment of 120,000 Japanese Americans during WWII.

💬 Bring a friend, bring your voice, and bring your appetite for pizza and progress.
